### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca186b3535e60ec83185de488c62a8748cbbe6a4` — the merge of head `1b90fa5f2abb38218c655a759b6b341d623c6414` into base `3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca186b3535e60ec83185de488c62a8748cbbe6a4 && git checkout ca186b3535e60ec83185de488c62a8748cbbe6a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b 1b90fa5f2abb38218c655a759b6b341d623c6414 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b && git merge --no-ff 1b90fa5f2abb38218c655a759b6b341d623c6414

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3543b51d37b41086275dacf91e7a29cb8c67da8b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e0b6fc402b1bc4d0de65ee98656746639a75e61f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-write-never-exceeds-delegator.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-enforce-parity.test.ts, .changeset/35917-by-id-widener-floor-term.md, content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts, content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx, content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx
Security-touching: yes

Read: card #35917 (body; triage 7049054086; claim 7061803234; os-dev-reports 7062563042 and 7064413744; decision analysis 7062795693; maintainer ruling 7063130499); PR #36117 (body, the 9-file list, the net diff against merge-base `493ad095d4`, +364/-60; `origin/main` was `78437e20d7`, one commit ahead, #36085, which does not touch the floor composition); the PR thread (docs-drift 7064420777); AGENTS.md (Prime Directive #14, Post-Task Checklist step 3) and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md`. Code outside the diff was read on the head. Nothing was built or run: every scenario below is derived by reading and none is measured. The ablation counts quoted are the dev's. Check-runs on the head at 15:10Z: 54 in all, 38 success, 15 skipped, 1 in progress (Test Core 3 of 10), none failed. I did not determine which shard carries plugin-security's suite. The PR is a draft; its `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

Result: PASS. No must-fix: I found no row writable at this head that ruling A does not admit, and no row refused that main admits. Open on this head: S1 to S4 (should-fix), N1 to N5 (nits). S1 answers the question the dev left to the seat: the #24792 guard still decides one region, a `controlled_by_parent` object, and nothing pins it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the floor decision is now.** With the knob set, `computeLayeredRlsFilter` keeps the whole collection, floor included, when the policies left after the floor would still compile to something: pass 1 drops one for a missing column, or one survives carrying a `using` (`security-plugin-rls-filter.ts:430-437`). `compileFilter` answers non-null exactly when a policy carries a predicate for the clause (`rls-compiler.ts:1090-1091`, `:1142`). So the floor is kept exactly where main's floor-dropped Layer 1 was non-null. Where main answered `null`, the head answers `null`. Where main answered a tree `X`, the head answers `floor OR X`, or the floor alone where `X` was the deny sentinel.
2. **The admitted set is the ruled one.** A by-id write newly passes Layer 1 only for a row that meets all three: the knob is set, which means the floor applies to the caller and the sharing verdict for this row and this write class is `allow` (`security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts:291-304`); a policy of floor provenance admits it (`created_by == current_user.id`, or an alternate a plugin contributed beside the floor); and every authored term refused it. Layer 0, the CRUD gate, the sharing middleware's own gate, the master gate and the field gates are ANDed as before.
3. **Nothing is narrowed.** Three hunks move behaviour.
   - Pre-image: a superset, by judgment 1.
   - `computeWriteCheckFilter` (`:687-691`): the head's `floorReplaced` implies main's. The two differ only when the knob is set, an authored `using` policy applies and no policy declares a `check`. There main's check was the OR of the authored `using`s and the head's is that OR plus the floor. Both lists are non-empty, so no absent check becomes a filter.
   - `checkAuthoredRowWrite` (`security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts:175-180`): the compiler sees the collection it saw on main. Alternates are materialised only beside a floor (`platform-ownership-policies.ts:165-194`), the pre-check at `:155-162` keeps the derive-from-select branch and the object default off, and the copy keeps every other member of the set. Same verdict.
   - With the knob unset (`abstain`, `deny`, the agent leg, every read), `withoutFloor` is `collected` and both functions take main's path. Pass 1 moved into a local function with the same body.
4. **Layer 0 / the tenant wall.** Not in the diff. It is computed apart from Layer 1 (`:498-507`) and ANDed; the probe still ANDs `layer0` (`security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts:185`). Pinned: the owner-creator's own closed row in another organization is refused by id and by predicate.
5. **ADR-0066 ①.** A Modify All holder on an ordinary object earns `allow`, the floor stays beside the authored term, and a row passes only if they created it or the authored term admits it. The pins hold all three: nothing when every row is closed, r2 and r3 when open, a closed row they created admitted. The always-true-term shape the analysis excluded would turn the first one red. On a posture-permitting object the short-circuit returns before this code (`:232`).
6. **Verb boundary (ADR-0111 D3).** `rlsOperationForVerb` picks `checkDelete` for the delete class, and `checkDelete` never answers `allow` on the strength of an `edit` share. So for a caller whose only basis is a share, the knob stays unset on a delete and the composition is main's. For a creator who holds only an `edit` share, the update is newly admitted (floor plus `allow`) and the delete is still refused by the sharing middleware, whose authored probe judges without the floor. CAROL's delete pin covers the probe; the share-holding creator has no pin (N4).
7. **Delegated callers.** The agent leg never sets the knob (`security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts:291`). The one delegated term that moves is the delegator's own composition (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1503-1511`). It is ANDed, and it is the composition the delegator's direct write gets, so an on-behalf-of write passes Layer 1 only where the delegator's own does. On an ordinary object that composition is now either the same tree as the floor-standing delegator filter beside it (`:1479-1481`) or `null`, so there it narrows nothing. See S1.
8. **The cbp master gate.** `assertMasterRowEditable` passes the knob into the same composition (`security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts:1229-1241`). A master the caller created and record sharing allows is now editable beside the master's authored update policy, so its details are writable: insert, update and delete, whoever created the detail rows. This is inside the option the maintainer picked (the analysis lists "master check"). It has no pin (S4), and the changeset's remedy does not reach it (S3).
9. **Explain/enforce parity.** Explain asks the same function with the same options (`security-plugin-explain-access.ts:339-346`, `:467-470`). Pinned for the owner-creator (r1 true, r4 false, both verbs) and in the two new parity rows.
10. **Check policies.** When any applicable policy declares a `check`, `writeCheckPolicies` returns only the declared ones and the floor has no part (`security-plugin.ts:1274-1283`); the EMEA control pins it. The floor's term in a defaulted check reads `created_by` from the image. That field is the platform's `system`, `readonly` audit field (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:346-347`), and the engine judges the stored row as well as the change set as sent, so a caller should not be able to pass the term by sending `created_by`. I read the declaration and did not trace the readonly strip for this field. The same term already stood in the `abstain` and `deny` compositions, so the exposure is not new.
11. **`abstain` and `deny`.** The knob is unset; both functions run main's path. Pinned on the owner-less memo (r1 and r3 on both paths, both verbs).
12. **The predicate path's #35914 relief.** `replaced` is null at the head exactly where it was on main (judgment 1), so the relief asks verdicts for the same writes. By id and by predicate now agree on the rows the floor admits. They do not agree on every row (S3).
13. **Non-SQL drivers.** Layer 1 gains one `$or` disjunct of the kind the knob-unset path already produced; the check runs in process. No new operator. Pinned on better-sqlite3 only.
14. **A fail-closed outcome moves, inside the ruled OR (information).** An authored write policy that cannot enforce (a missing column, an unresolved membership key) used to deny every by-id write under `allow`. The creator's rows now pass by the floor, as they already did under `abstain` and by predicate.

### ② Semver level

- **Level.** `'@objectstack/plugin-security': patch` is right: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a widening ships `patch` with no ADR-0087 marker.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on the PR body and the changeset (`:7-8`). The widening arm is right: judgment 3 finds no narrowing. `none` is the reading in the analysis the maintainer ruled on (no key moves, and the spec's OR text is unchanged).
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.**

| Sentence | Verdict |
|:---|:---|
| Summary (`:5`) | True. |
| The defect (`:10`) | True as the dev measured it at the engine door. An `edit` share earns `allow` on an update only (N2). |
| The ruling (`:12`) | Matches comment 7063130499. |
| "dropped only where it is the filter's last term … row gate … defaulted check" (`:14`) | True. "An authored write policy" means one with a `using`: beside a check-only policy the floor is still the last term and is dropped. |
| "admitted again" (`:16`) | True for the class. The parenthesis leaves out two bases (N2). |
| "a creator who does not own the row is still refused by it" (`:16`) | False as written: S3. |
| "By id and by predicate now admit the same rows" (`:16`) | False as written: S3. |
| Explain and the master check (`:17`) | True by reading. Explain is pinned; the master check is not (S4). |
| The delegated write and the 22 tests (`:19`) | True by reading; 12 and 10 match the diff. "An agent still never writes a row its delegator's own write refuses" holds by reading, and on a cbp object it rests on the guard S1 names. |
| "Removed capability" and the remedy (`:21`) | The loss is stated correctly. The remedy is incomplete: S3. `beforeDelete` is the home the spec names for delete-time guards (`packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts:50`). |
| "What does not change" (`:25-30`) | True, each of the six. |

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (dev report 7062563042): A, B or C.** Ruled A by the maintainer (7063130499). The build matches the option as the analysis describes it: row gate, defaulted check, explain, master check.
- **Out-of-scope finding: an OPEN row the caller neither owns nor holds a share on is admitted by id and left out of a predicate write.** Real, and not this PR's: by id it is the #5493 authored lift of the sharing refusal, and the bulk half was closed as not planned (#6736). The head's own test records it (`predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts:566`, `:569`). It should be filed or deduped by the seat, and it makes one changeset sentence false (S3).
- **Out-of-scope finding: the #24792 guard has no discriminating pin.** Confirmed, and narrower than reported: S1.
- **#35934 and the cbp half of #35802.** Out of scope, as the dev says. #35934's case (iv) stays true at this head (judgment 12).
- **The jsdoc breach.** Acceptable. It is one line (`security-plugin.ts:635`), the analysis the ruling adopts names that exact line as owed, the PR body declares it, and the sentence is accurate. A second docblock in the same file is now stale (N1).
- **Tier (information).** The diff touches no published schema and no governed path; `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` leaves the face to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which reads `yes (widening)`. This record is at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER because claim 7061803234 orders that tier.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. The by-id re-read carries one more pushed-down disjunct.
- **File surface.** Eight paths are inside claim 7061803234; the ninth is the declared jsdoc line. No exported symbol moves.
- **Docs.** `sharing-rules.mdx:76-82` is true. A second page states the old composition (S2).

### ④ Design judgment

**The 22 rewritten tests.** Every assertion is kept verbatim; the diff changes row tuples and comments and adds cells. Each test's stated invariant still holds. What each half can detect changed:

| Tests | Rows, before and after | The delegator's own half | The on-behalf-of half |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| D10 `held_1`, `held_2`, delete (6 tests) | creator BOUNDED, now OTHER; `held_2` also owner OTHER | Real: remove the authored policy and the floor is the last term, `allow` drops it, the row is admitted. | Refused by the delegator's floor-standing filter with or without the authored policy. The same shape as the `plain_*` cells. |
| D10 `d_held`, detail delete (4 tests) | master `m_held` creator BOUNDED, now OTHER | Real, through the master gate. | As above, on the delegator's pass of the master gate. |
| D10 store test (2 tests) | `store_*` creator BOUNDED, now OTHER | Real: the defaulted check refuses the `held` image. | Refused by the delegator's floor-standing check. |
| Parity `p_bounded_held`, `p_del_bounded_held`, `d_under_bounded_held` (10 tests) | creator D_BOUNDED, now D_OTHER | Real, and explain equals enforce. | Explain equals enforce still holds. The refusal is the floor's, the shape `p_org_mine_created_by_other` already pins. |

None was weakened to pass: the old rows pinned the outcome the ruling reversed, and moving them is the remedy the analysis prescribes. But no on-behalf-of half can now tell a tree with the #24792 guard from one without it, which is the dev's G1 to G3 reading (0 red at the head, against 4, 2 and 6 on the control leg). On an ordinary object no fixture could, by judgment 7. See S1.

**The new pins.**

| Pin | Result |
|:---|:---|
| ALICE, update and delete, all closed and r2 open | Real. Red under A1; the update cases red under A2. |
| BOB, DAVE, the Modify All holder, all closed | Real as controls for the bound that must stay: BOB and the Modify All holder go red under the always-true term the analysis excluded. Green under A1 to A3 by design. |
| CAROL, both verbs | Real: red under A3, where the floor would answer the probe as an authored admission. |
| The Modify All holder's own created closed row | Real. Red under A1 and A2. |
| The EMEA `check` control | Real. Its refusing half is a control; its admitting half is red under A1. |
| The tenant wall, the owner-less memo | Real as controls. |
| Explain r1 and r4 | Real. r1 is red under A1. |
| `held_created` cells and parity rows | Real. Red under A1 (the dev's 8 of 192). |

**Ablations.** A1 to A3 each name the anchor, the red counts match what the code predicts, and the restore is shown. Credible. G1 to G3 are the right instrument and were reported, not hidden. Not ablated, and no pin would go red: the `rest.dropped` leg of the floor decision (N3), the master check (S4), a creator who holds an `edit` share (N4).

**Design.** Keeping the collection whole is the smallest change that makes the by-id door the predicate door's composition, and asking "would an authored term remain" through the compile's own pass 1 keeps the two from disagreeing. Taking the floor out of the probe's sets, not through the knob, is what keeps the floor from answering as an authored admission. What gives way is listed below.

S1 (should-fix) — the #24792 guard is still the only thing holding ADR-0090 D10 on a `controlled_by_parent` object, and no test pins it. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1503-1511`, `:2253-2261`; `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts:1252-1267`; `delegated-write-never-exceeds-delegator.test.ts:9-14`, `:178-193`; PR body, Acceptance notes, first bullet.

Where it narrows, by reading: only where the delegator's own composition carries the `masterGateCoversThisWrite` vouch and the floor-standing delegator filter does not. That is a cbp object: the written detail for the pre-image and check sites, a cbp middle master for the master-gate site. The PR body also names "an OWD that opens row writes". That half is wrong: `platformFloorYieldsToObjectWriteModel` answers for `public_read_write` from the object alone (`security-plugin.ts:4524`), so both delegator filters drop the floor there and the guard narrows nothing.

Scenario: a cbp detail, a delegator D holding an authored update policy on it (`note != 'held'`), a detail row D created whose note is `held`, under a master D may edit.

- D's own by-id update: the floor yields to the master gate, the authored policy alone decides, refused.
- An agent on D's behalf: the agent's own leg does not refuse a row D created (the `free_1` and `d_free` controls are admitted on its behalf); the floor-standing delegator filter admits the row by `created_by`; the master gate admits. Only the guard refuses.
- Delete the guard as redundant (on an ordinary object it now is) and the suite stays green while the agent writes a row D's own write refuses. That is #24746 again.

Not a must-fix: the guard's code is untouched and no row is wrongly admitted at this head. It is owed here because this PR's rewrite is what removed its pins, and the file's header still says it pins "the one the delegator's OWN direct write sets". Fix: the D10 rig already has a cbp `DETAIL`. Add an update policy on it to `qa_bounded_writer`, a detail created by BOUNDED that the policy refuses, a cell with both outcomes refused, and a store variant for the check site; ablate G1 and G2 and report the reds. The master-gate site needs a cbp middle master; pin it or file it. Correct the header and the PR body note.

S2 (should-fix) — a second docs page still states the composition this PR replaces. `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx:61-64`.

It reads: "A by-id write takes that replacement, and so does a predicate write unless an app-authored `using` policy for the write applies to the caller (then it keeps the floor beside that policy)." That is the sentence the PR rewrote in `sharing-rules.mdx:76-79`; here it still says a by-id write under an authored policy loses the floor. The two pages now contradict each other, the page is inside the claim's surface (`content/docs/permissions/**`), and the docs-drift check lists it (7064420777). Also owed by the analysis the ruling adopts and absent: one sentence in the RLS page saying a write policy adds rows and where a cap goes; `rls.mdx:79-82` still says an authored update predicate "decides the `update` filter alone".

S3 (should-fix) — four statements about what this PR admits and removes are wrong or incomplete. `.changeset/35917-by-id-widener-floor-term.md:16`, `:21`; `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx:80-82`.

- "a creator who does not own the row is still refused by it" (`:16`). True only for a creator with no sharing basis. A creator with write depth over the owner, Modify All, or an `edit` share on an update gets `allow` and is now admitted. The PR shows it: `held_2` was owner OTHER, creator BOUNDED, an `org`-depth writer, and had to move to OTHER and OTHER to stay refused.
- "By id and by predicate now admit the same rows" (`:16`). The head's own test has the predicate write change r1 and r2 and the by-id oracle admit r1 to r4 on the same object and policy (`predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts:566`, `:569`). Scope the sentence to the rows the floor admits and name the divergence.
- The remedy (`:21`, docs `:80-82`). A `check` judges the stored image, so it does not hold a creator's row in a state. Scenario: an author froze closed deals with `using: "stage != 'closed'"`, follows the docs and adds `check: "stage != 'closed'"`; the creator-owner sends `{ stage: 'open', amount: 1 }` on a closed deal; the floor admits the row, the image passes the check, the deal is re-opened and edited. By id before this PR that write was refused. The analysis names three homes for an update cap (a `check`, a validation rule, a stage-conditioned field lock); the prose names one. Say what a `check` bounds, and name a home that reads the row as it stood before the write: a `beforeUpdate` hook has it as `ctx.previous` (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts:1066`).
